new_statements.quote: [p. 207] In Pacaraos Quechua (see section 3.2.9) stress is phonemic. It may lie either on the penultimate or on the final syllable. Word-final stress in Pacaraos is either due to the elision of a final syllable, for instance, in aksti-k, from aksti-kta (potato-AC), or to a word-final occurrence of the first-person marker -'y. Otherwise, penultimate stress is predominant. [p. 243] Phonologically, Pacaraos Quechua presents the particularity of a phonemic stress distinction involving a choice between final and penultimate syllables. Final stress is a characteristic of the first-person marker -y, as in tarpity 'I sow'

new_statements.relation_note: The catalog row for 'quechua de Pacaraos' has an empty rule and there are no existing statements, so this is the first placement statement: predominant penultimate stress with morphologically conditioned final stress (phonemic contrast). Quotes are verbatim API scanned: 'aksti-k'/'aksti-kta' = aksu-k/aksu-kta, 'tarpity' = tarpúy, -'y = -´y. Book itself not downloadable (controlled lending); the deciding paragraphs were reconstructed in full from overlapping full-text-search snippets, page numbers fixed by running-header snippets.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Penultimate stress is the rule ('predominant', 'the rule in Pacaraos Quechua'), but stress is phonemic/contrastive because two morphological sources put stress on the final syllable: (a) the first-person marker -´y when word-final (tarpúy 'I sow'; §3.2.3: 'a segment -y that attracts stress to the preceding vowel when it occurs in word-final position'), and (b) elision of a final syllable, e.g. aksú-k from aksu-kta 'potato-ACC' (also 'a number of other suffixes that are subject to elision when in word-final position'; the -s allomorph passage: 'When the allomorph -s occurs in word-final position, the vowel preceding it is stressed'). Fn. 24 calls this 'the essentially penultimate stress of Pacaraos Quechua' and uses it against Torero's view that an Ancash-type pattern is Proto-Quechua.
new_statements.exceptions: Final stress with word-final first-person -´y and after elision of a final syllable/suffix (contrastive with penultimate stress in otherwise identical strings); the family-wide statement on p. 206 also allows word-final stress in interjections and emphatic expressions (alaláw 'how cold!').
new_statements.identity_note: The sketch (§3.2.9, pp. 242-249) describes the Quechua of the village of Pacaraos (district capital, upper Chancay valley, Lima department), which the authors treat as a separate dialect intermediate between Quechua I and Quechua IIC ('some authors prefer to associate it with Quechua I (Parker 1969d: 191-2)'); the p. 207 statement is about the same variety. Field data from Adelaar's own 1979 fieldwork (story told by the late Mrs Lorena Cordova).
